At ALU, we’re not just teaching; we’re nurturing the leaders who will drive Africa’s progress and prosperity in the 21st century We are dedicated to fostering an open yet secure environment, balancing the safety of students, staff, and visitors with respect for individual rights, and safeguarding responsibilities. HOW WE WORK The ALU Team works in starkly different ways to traditional academic bureaucracies. We approach education from first principles, empower individuals to design, test, and implement creative new ideas, and work closely together to craft transformative learning experiences. We are deeply passionate about our students and excited by the challenge of building something entirely new. The African Leadership University is committed to ensuring the safety and Well-being of all students under our care. As part of this commitment , we have a comprehensive safeguarding policy in place , which outlines our Zero-tolerance approach to any violation of safeguarding. ABOUT WCN Wildlife Conservation Network’s mission is to protect endangered wildlife by supporting conservationists who ensure wildlife and people coexist and thrive. Within WCN, the Women for Wildlife (WfW) program supports conservation partners in Africa to implement gender-focused programs to achieve conservation benefits through women’s empowerment. ABOUT THE ROLE The Wildlife Conservation Network (WCN) created the WfW grants program to support their partners in Africa to build and strengthen their gender-focused programs for the dual goals of women‘s empowerment and conservation benefit. Partners who are successful in applying for WfW funding will join a Community of Learning for the purpose of: Encouraging and sharing innovative and holistic approaches to conservation and gender-related challenges, Supporting and mentoring women and female leaders working in the field, and facilitating partnerships and mutual capacity building between organizations Gathering data, knowledge and lessons that will inform further rounds of women-focused granting and grantee management Tracking and evaluating progress and impact of grantee activities as it pertains to women- focussed programming Creating and implementing best practices for gender rights and equity in conservation and development. Building capacity within partners for effective and ethical gender-related programming. Community of Learning activities will take place over a 12 month period and include: An initial qualitative needs assessment with each incoming grantee to assess strengths, areas of expertise, and self identified areas for growth in relation to gender-focused programming Creation and maintenance of a basic digital platform (such as a Whatsapp or Slack channel), and facilitation of communication and engagement on the platform to promote sustained information-gathering and sharing of knowledge between grantees Creation of a pathway of learning for grantees, including a remote curriculum and facilitated practical work that increases the capacity of organizations to carry out grounded and effective gender empowerment work Hosting of 8 virtual gatherings design and implementation of methods for impact evaluation of grantee’s projects and the network overall, based on goals specific to the grantee as well as overarching goals of the WoW initiative. Design and implementation of methods for self assessment of gender equity and gender-related rights in the implementation of grant-supported projects and within grantee organizations. To support the design and implementation of the WoW Community of Learning, WCN seeks a candidate to take the role of Curriculum Development Intern Nature and scope of work: Curriculum design, including background research and creation of learning materials and tools Documentation of emerging learning and development of this into new learning tools and products Design and maintenance of digital platforms for delivery of curriculum, and facilitation of communication and knowledge-sharing activities on those platforms Design and coordination of virtual curriculum gatherings Skills needed: Curriculum design Evaluation of educational curricula Proficiency in written and spoken English Proficiency on digital platforms including Whatsapp, Slack, ZOOM, Google docs Proficiency with software programs including Microsoft Word, Excel and Powerpoint Strong interpersonal skills and excellent verbal and written communication Skills Development plan: Curriculum Design Evaluation of educational curricula-although a basic level of experience and comfort with these skill sets is required, the candidate can expect to develop further proficiency in these skills as well as an advanced knowledge of the content being taught the curricula themselves. Number of vacancies: 2 Location: Remote Working Hours: 20 Start Date: November 15, 2026 End Date: November 15, 2027 Deadline of application: October 15, 2026

items.description: We are seeking a Public Policy & Government Relations Lead / Coordinator - Brazil to join Foggo Entertainment and support our operations in Brazil. This role will focus on government relations, public policy, and external stakeholder engagement across the local, state, and federal levels. The successful candidate will develop and maintain strong relationships with policymakers, regulators, government representatives, industry associations, and other key external stakeholders, while supporting Foggo’s business and policy priorities in Brazil. This is a field-facing role that requires a strong understanding of the Brazilian public policy and regulatory landscape, as well as availability to travel to Foggo’s headquarters and other locations across Brazil when required. What You’ll Do Government Relations & Stakeholder Engagement: Develop and maintain strong relationships with federal, state, and particularly local government leaders in areas where Foggo operates. Public Policy Strategy: Lead and implement public affairs and public policy strategies aligned with Foggo’s business objectives in Brazil. Regulatory Monitoring: Assess and communicate potential regulatory and policy risks and opportunities, developing appropriate mitigation strategies and policy positions. External Advocacy: Coordinate government outreach, external advocacy programs, and key public policy initiatives. Government Support: Provide government relations and public affairs support to Foggo teams to help ensure smooth business operations. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with internal teams including Business Development, Legal, Compliance, Payments, Finance, and external PR partners. External Communications: Effectively communicate the scope, impact, and benefits of Foggo’s investments and operations to external stakeholders at different levels and across different areas of expertise. Representation: Represent Foggo in meetings and engagements with government authorities, regulators, industry organizations, and other relevant stakeholders. Reporting Line & Work Setup Reports to: Head of Legal, Regulatory, IGR & DPO, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Director of Compliance and Institutional Relations. Work Setup: This is a remote position. However, due to the nature of the role and its focus on government relations, public policy, and engagement with federal authorities and other institutional stakeholders, the position is expected to be based in Brasília, DF. The role also requires availability to travel to Foggo’s headquarters and other locations across Brazil as needed. Solid experience in Public Policy, Government Relations, Public Affairs, Community Relations, Corporate Social Responsibility, or a related field. Bachelor’s degree in Law, Political Science, Public Policy, Public Affairs, Economic Development, or a related discipline. Fluency in Portuguese and English (written and verbal) required. Proven experience in Government Relations and Public Policy within the Brazilian gaming/iGaming sector or another highly regulated industry. Strong experience building and managing relationships with government representatives, regulators, industry associations, and other external stakeholders. Ability to assess regulatory and policy developments, identify potential risks and opportunities, and develop appropriate policy and stakeholder engagement strategies. Nice-to-Haves (Advantages) Spanish language proficiency. Master’s degree or above in a relevant discipline. Strong track record of building and managing coalitions with industry associations, think tanks, advocacy organizations, or similar stakeholders in Brazil and Latin America. Experience working across local, state, and federal government levels in Brazil. Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic environment with changing priorities and regulatory requirements. Health Insurance Meal Voucher Transportation Allowance Paid Time-off

items.title: Creative (Graphic Designer)
items.summary: Superside is looking for a talented Graphic Designer to join our global creative team. You'll create standout visual work for some of the world's most ambitious brands: from brand identity and campaign design to digital and social assets. You’ll be working alongside creative leads, project managers, and clients across a wide range of industries. This is a hands-on design role built for the way design actually gets made today. You'll spend most of your time designing, building concepts, refining visual systems, and pushing craft, using today's leading AI creative tools as a core part of your process, not an afterthought. We're looking for designers who already treat tools & models like Flora, Krea, Figma AI, Claude, NanoBanana, GPT Image, and Seedance as part of their everyday kit, and who know when to reach for them and when strong traditional craft is what the work actually needs.

items.title: Creative (Motion Design)
items.summary: Superside is looking for a motion designer with the creativity, technical expertise, and innovation mindset to push the boundaries of motion design. You’ll work with top global brands, crafting high-impact motion graphics, animated digital ads, Lottie animations, and more, all while collaborating with a world-class, globally distributed team of creatives. This is a high-ownership role where you’ll contribute to cutting-edge projects, explore new animation technologies, and help shape Superside’s creative motion capabilities.
